I am 33 and have farmed these fields in Quzhou since I was a boy. I never went to school, but I know what this land needs. Here, the safe thing is winter wheat followed by summer maize — that is what my father did, and what all my neighbors do. I have about 8 mu of good flat land, and I will put all of it into the wheat–maize rotation this year.

My wheat is already in the ground from last October. I rotary-tilled the soil before sowing and used about 30 jin of improved wheat seed per mu — half saved from my own harvest, half bought from the township seed station. I spread about 100 jin of compound fertilizer as basal dressing and will topdress with urea once in spring. I will irrigate three times: at green-up, jointing, and grain filling. I will spray four times in total — insecticide twice, herbicide once, and fungicide once — because rust and aphids are always a threat. I expect about 1,000 jin per mu.

As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, I will plant hybrid maize on the same 8 mu without plowing again. No-tillage saves diesel and time, and the hybrids from the seed shop grow fast and strong. I will apply about 80 jin of compound fertilizer at sowing, irrigate twice during the trumpet leaf and grain-filling stages, and spray pesticide three times — twice for insects and once for weeds. I expect about 1,100 jin per mu.

I thought about planting cotton on a couple of mu, but the labor is heavy and the market price bounces around too much. I also thought about vegetables, but without a greenhouse or a guaranteed buyer, that is gambling. Wheat and maize prices are steady, the grain station always buys them, and I know exactly how to grow them. That is my plan.
